In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/28/2023
Violation Code: 78a85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - The operator failed to prevent gas flow in the annulus. In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.
Violation ID: 8165425
Permit API: 015-23768
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Troy Township
Inspection Type: Plugging(Includes Plugged/Mined Through)
Inspection Date: 11/09/2023
Comments: An inspection of the Cummings Lumber 9H well was conducted on November 9, 2023 at 10:50 am. At the time of inspection, the rig is rigging down after plugging operations and the operator is in the process of pouring gravel in the surface section of the wellbore above all plugs. This process was ceased temporarily for the evaluation and inspection of the well at this time. Approximately 3-4% methane and 60% LEL was detected at the top of the well casing with an Altair 5x gas meter at this time. Additionally, approximately 2000 PPM-M was detected with a Remote Methane Leak Detector (RMLD). The operator has reported no pressure or gas detected during recent internal inspections. It was theorized at this time that pouring of gravel may be displacing the static gas in the wellbore, causing it to vacate the wellbore and detectable at surface. It was decided at this time to continue filling the wellbore with gravel and re-inspect. Continued pouring gravel at 11:15 am. They finished pouring gravel at 12:00:pm. Reinspected well; no elevated gas was detected at the top of the well with RMLD (see attached photos), no gas was detected with Altair 5x gas meter at the top of the well at the time of inspection . The operator plans to cut plugged well below ground level and bury to finalize plugging at this time. Repsol will be submitting a signed Certificate of Well Plugging including an "As Plugged" well-bore schematic with further plugging details.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr ¿Stepped¿ pressure build-up tests ¿SPBUT¿ being performed on all (5)wells on the HUNTER pad. The HUNTER 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H wells. These tests are being performed in response to a gas migration investigation in area underway by The Department. SPBUTs were initiated on 5/26/20 @ ~ 08:15 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - All (5) wells on the pad are shut in w/ Frac valves installed on top of well heads. Starting at approx. 10:15, ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Op. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/11/2026 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Redstone Township, Fayette county. 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/11/2026
Violation Code: 102.11(a)1 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS – BMP AND DESIGN STANDARDS - Person failed to design, implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation to protect, maintain, reclaim and restore water quality and existing and designated uses.
Violation ID: 8267703
Permit API: 051-21986
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Redstone Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/11/2026
Comments: On March 11, 2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection of the Gabonay National City Bank 6 well in response to the operator's submission of a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well. This inspection is being separated into 3 inspection reports due to the number of photos taken. The narrative of all 3 inspection reports are identical except for the references to photos. This is inspection report 1 of 3.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. At this time, plugging operations have not yet commenced and there is currently no rig on-site. Earth disturbance for site preparation has commenced. E and S plan is present on-site at the mailbox at the beginning of the access road.Well is tagged and posted. Production tank is observed within an adequately vegetated berm at this time. No spills, leaks, or releases are observed at this time. The RCE is not installed as depicted on the plans. Minimal gravel is observed, which appears to be pre-existing. The access road does not appear to be graveled by the operator despite the E and S plans calling for the road to be "graveled as necessary." Four locations on the access road are experiencing erosion and sedimentation off of the access road (Photos 10-13, 18). CFS is also not observed in these locations despite the E and S plan call for CFS installed "as needed."There are 8 culvert crossings observed during today's inspection. Some ends of the culverts are blocked due to what appears to be recent soil and vegetation clearing off the access road. Some of the culvert crossings appear to possibly be stream crossings. A follow up inspection is being requested with Department Biologists to identify possible streams and/or wetlands. CFS is not observed to be installed at any of the culvert crossings except for the last culvert crossing closest to the site. The CFS at this crossing appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time, but is only installed on one side of the crossing. The E and S plans on site do not delineate or identify any stream or wetlands or crossings of any streams or wetlands, and no 105 permits are observed on site or at any of the crossings at this time. The Department recommends the operator install controls in accordance with the construction sequence and the E and S plan.CFS is observed to be installed on-site near the well and appears to be installed and functioning properly at this time. The location of the CFS appears to be placed in the correct area in relation to the site's topography, however the E and S plans depict the CFS to be placed on the opposite (East) side of the site. A small channel of stormwater appears to be leaving the site and passing through CFS at this time, however no sediment is observed leaving the site. The Department recommends the operator monitor and maintain this area as necessary to ensure CFS continues to function properly. Plastic matting is observed to be installed in 3 locations along the access road.The Department recommends the operator redline the site plans to appropriately match on-site field changes.Violations are being issued for accelerated erosion and sedimentation off of the access road, for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S plan, and for failing to maintain access road culverts. Additional violations may be forthcoming pending consultation with Department Biologists.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PIN OAK ENERGY PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/15/2022
Violation Code: 78a65(a)1i - SITE RESTORATION - Post Drilling - Owner or operator failed to restore the land surface within 9 months after completion of drilling all permitted wells on the well site or 9 months after the expiration of all existing well permits on the well site, whichever is later.
Violation ID: 948184
Permit API: 047-24642
Unconventional: Yes
County: Elk
Municipality: Jones Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/15/2022
Comments: This unconventional well is currently equipped for production and is equipped with a well tag displaying the well’s API number. The site ID sign at the entrance of the pad includes the required information, however it has become faded. Drilling operations were completed on this well on 1/6/2012. Pin Oak has failed to restore this well site according to approved plans associated with ESX11-047-0026 and more than nine months have passed since the completion of drilling the last permitted well on this well site. Approximately one-half of this pad does not appear to be actively used for the operation of this well. There are two steel tanks labeled as holding production water located inside of a lined steel containment on this well site. At this time, the containment appears sound, as it is holding several inches of stormwater. The access road leading to this well site is in general holding up to current traffic levels. There are isolated areas of scouring that should be addressed in an effort to avoid potential E&S issues in the future. Routine maintenance/improvements to the road surface should be considered prior to any heavy equipment use of the road given its proximity to Bear Creek, Slide Run, Little Wolf Run and several unnamed tributaries. Vegetative cover around the perimeter of the well site and the access road banks appears to be established. Future inspections will be conducted during the upcoming growing season to further evaluate the stabilization of earth disturbance associated with this well site.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2023
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. Onsite with DEP staff Alicia Furey and Lucas Eichner to collect a water sample from the earthen dike. The earthen dike is retaining fluid inside the bottom of the entire dike. There is approximately 4-5" of oily water pooled inside the dike. The dike drain remains closed and plugged. Water flowing into a separator barrel on top of a steel oil tank could be heard from the ground.Prior to the site visit water samples of the Bellows Spring was collected for analysis. There are 4 separate pipes flowing water into the cistern for the spring. Each pipe was identified, labeled, and sampled separately.After collecting samples from the earthen dike, DEP staff walked the hillside between the tank battery and Bellows Spring. The goal was to investigate any other oil and gas activity that may be located above the spring and that would be a potential contributor to the impact of the Bellows Spring. There was nothing observed between the tank battery and the Bellows Spring relating to oil and gas activity.At 2:05pm Mr. Rhoades was called via phone by the Department. The current condition of the tank battery was discussed with Mr. Rhoades and he indicated that a water truck is scheduled for next week to empty the dike and the brine tanks. Mr. Rhoades also stated that he has hired Moody and Associates as a consultant and that a check was in the mail to obtain their services. The Department clearly communicated the importance and urgency of starting the cleanup process at the site including the earthen dike area. Mr. Rhoades seemed to understand and asked if the water was good to drink yet in Reno and if individual households are being tested. I explained to Mr. Rhoades that samples have been taken from the spring by Oil and Gas Operations and that I was unaware of any other sampling/testing. It was also stated that the "Do not Consume" advisory has not yet been lifted from my knowledge at the time. The phone call was concluded with Mr. Rhoades indicating that he is starting the process to clean things up.

Comments: On November 26, 2019, I conducted a follow up inspection related to a release of material reported to the Department on 11/23/2019. I was accompanied by PADEP OGI John Rushin and Range Resources representatives Nate Smiell, John Fountain. Nick Reda and Matthew Kravitis. At the time of inspection, the impacted area was excavated to an approximated depth of 7 feet. The excavated area was approximately 30'x25'. I was able to see all sides of the corrugated steel well cellar and surrounding bed rock material. It appears that the impacted material has been removed but will be confirmed with sampling as the Operator continues to follow the spill policy. I did observe a significant crack in the bedrock below the 5H cellar. Mr. Smiell measured the crack and it was found to be approximately 79” in length and approximately 15” deep. The crack was approximately 2” wide. This could be a potential pathway to groundwater and the Operator should continue to monitor the key way drains and surface waters as a precaution. Additionally, the Operator has updated the amount of OBM released from 3 barrels to 5 barrels. The impacted material removed from the well pad was placed in 15 roll off boxes awaiting disposal. PADEP John Rushin was onsite and discussed additional issued related to the cement returns with the 5H and 6H wells. Violations remain outstanding and additional violations may be forthcoming as part of the Departments investigation.

Comments: On May 15, 2025 the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of the Louis Yemc 1 plugged well site located in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County in response to IR 3894560 where violations were continued for failure to restore the well site. Violation ID: 8197139

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/05/2024
Comments: On August 5 2024, the Department responded to an incident occuring in Fayette County, Washington Township. On August 5 2024 at 11:25am, the Department received a report that around 11:00am a truck on loading produced water from the production tanks had equipment malfunction resulting in an estimate of over 5 gallons spilling onto the ground. An EQT representative stated that it spilled on the ground but did not get into the waterways of commonwealth. At the time of this inspection, Act 9 Sign was present but faded. The Department recommends that the Operator update the Act 9 Sign as appropriate to ensure compliance with 78a55. At the time of this inspection, a third party representative of EQT (Specialized Professional Services Inc.) was completing clean up of the affected area. Equipment was present. Excavation was actively occurring during this inspection. The affected area was near the off loading and on/off loading area of the production tanks. According to a SPSI representative, a truck was unloading production fluid from the production tanks and had a failure at the connection, which caused production fluid to spill near the on/off loading site and visually extended down the side of the access road roughly 50ft. The SPSI representative stated that roughly 10 to 15 gallons spilled. Soil conductivity readings as well as a background soil conductivity reading was taken. The background soil conductivity reading was 0.1145mS. Soil conductivity readings were taken within the affected area were 0.458mS, 0.0031mS, and 0.0979mS. One reading in the visually affected area was elevated above the background reading of 0.1145mS. The Department recommends that the Operator remediate the fluid release in accordance with 78a.66. The Department also requests the Operator evaluate the release that has occurred and provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred, to be provided in the requested NOV Response. The Department also requests waste manifests upon proper disposal of wastes generated from the spill remediation.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued at this time.

Comments: On 02/01/2021, DEP representative John Ciccone conducted an administrative report for Chesapeake Appalachia LLC's (CALLC) STONE BRA location. This location is currently in flowback operations after fracking the STONE N 3HC and STONE N 104HC wells. This report is in response to a spill notification (CTS # 354624) received on 01/30/2021 at 0900 hours. The purpose of this report is to document details regarding the reported release, remediation actions taken thus far by CALLC, and to cite violations. On 01/30/2021, Tony Savitski (CALLC) reported that at 0900 hours, a mixture of rainwater and produced water spilled to the pad surface due to a hole in a containment structure. An estimated 42 gallons was reported as released. An estimated 20' x 20' area of impacted soils has been excavated and stored on containment, pending sample results for proper disposal. It was reported that no fluid escaped from the pad. On 02/01/2021, I contacted Eric Hottenstein (CALLC) at 0845 hours in order to gather more details regarding the release. Mr. Hottenstein stated that a frac tank storing produced fluids and stationed within secondary containment leaked fluid into containment. A hole in containment, believed to be caused by a hose puncture, resulted in the mixture of rainwater and produced fluid to leak to the pad surface. Mr. Hottenstein estimated that approximately 10 tons of impacted soils had been excavated and stored in containment. Mr. Hottenstein stated CALLC plans to pursue ACT 2 remediation. Samples for ACT 2 purposes have been collected and the frac tank containment has reportedly been fixed. Photos of the site have been forwarded by Mr. Hottenstein and attached to this report. The release of 42 gallons of the rainwater and produced fluid is in violation of Pa. Code 78a.56(a), CSL 402(b), and SWMA 301. Due to the quantity of the reported release, it is requested that CALLC refer to and remediate in accordance with Pa. Code 78a.66. This release is referred to the DEP's Bureau of Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields.

This inspection is to report the results of one water sample that was collected from a water/mud puddle east of the well heads.During an inspection on 3/8/2023, the department discovered high conductance fluid on the well pad surface outside of containment. The fluid covered a 20' x 60' area and field tested at 13.01 mS conductance with an Oakton PCTS-50 meter. The department collected water sample #9551-046 for laboratory analysis from location Lat: 41.66531 Long: -76.126427. On 4/4/2023 the department received the results of the laboratory analysis that shows elevated barium, strontium and lithium and is indicative of brine/production fluid being released onto the pad. The sample report is displayed in pictures 1 and 2. Chesapeake is pursuing Act 2 for the site in response to that incident.The release of fluid with elevated conductance to the pad surface constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and 78.66(b)(2).Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3492400 for elevated conductance fluid being discovered on the unprotected pad surface and for inspection ID 3517302 for elevated conductance fluid being discovered on the unprotected pad surface.

Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 78a85(a)5 - CASING AND CEMENTING - CEMENT STANDARDS - The operator failed to prevent gas flow in the annulus. In areas of known shallow gas producing zones, gas block additives and low fluid loss slurries shall be used.

Permit API: 115-22250
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Harford Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/23/2022
Comments: At time of inspection. There were twelve wells on site, the Jeffers Farm P2 7H, 8H, 9H, 10H, 11H, 12H, 13H, 14H, 15H, 16H, 17H, 18H and all of the wells were active. The well was set up for automated production. There was water 5.5' below grade in the cellar with no bubbling noticed and there was no gas detected in the remainder of the cellar. There was no gas detected in the vicinity of the well or the GPUs. All gas checks were conducted with a MSA Altair 5X multi gas detector that was calibrated on 11/21/22. I took a walk around the location and there were no obvious concerns noticed. There were no new violations noted.
